## Benedict Leonardi

Graduate Student in Economics · Lindner College of Business, University of Cincinnati\
*Wolfgang-Mayer Fellow in Economics*

---

My primary interests lie in **urban and regional economics** — the spatial organization of cities, the economics of public infrastructure, and how institutional arrangements shape access to opportunity. In my broader approach I strive to be interdisciplinary, anchored in empirical analysis and enriched by historical and philosophical inquiry.

My work examines how normative commitments influence both the development and interpretation of economic models, and how classical and medieval moral theories intersect with contemporary economic assumptions.

Prior work includes grant-funded research on mathematics education, studies examining local tax policy and public transit finance, and digital humanities projects using natural language processing on historical texts.
